newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court says Italian bread import rules violate EC treaty.
newsitem.headline: Court says Italian bread import rules violate EC treaty.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Thursday Italy cannot prohibit local sales of bread manufactured in France, even if the bread does not meet Italian moisture and ash content rules.
The court said Italy's rule is a trade barrier between member states, violates the EC treaty prohibition against trade restriction and is not justified by a need to protect the public's health.
The Italian magistrate in Pordenone, Italy, brought charges against an Italian resident distributing bread manufactured in France by the firm BCS, based in Tarascon.
The bread, certified of good quality in France, was imported by Soveda into Italy, and sold to supermarkets.
The Italian health officials said the bread infringed local law because its moisture content was too high, its ash content too low, and it contained bran.
The manufacture and marketing of bread are not areas currently harmonized by EU rules.
This ruling is consistent with the court's decisions in earlier cases not to honour member state rules restricting imports of bread because of salt or dry matter contents.
The court noted that the Italian Ministry for Industry, Commerce and Crafts has a rule in effect which amends Italian law and permits bread not conforming to Italian standards to be imported.
The court told the Italian magistrate to drop charges against the distributor which are based on restrictive trade policies.
EXCERPTS FROM THE JUDGMENT
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: Italian)
"Articles 30 and 36 of the Treaty - Composition of bread - Maximum moisture content, minimum ash content and prohibition of certain ingredients"
Case C-358/95
Reference from the Pretura de Pordenone (Italy) for a preliminary ruling in the proceedings pending before that court between
Tommaso Morellato
and
Unita Sanitaria Locale (USL) No 11, Pordenone
on the interpretation of articles 30 and 36 of the EC Treaty
THE COURT hereby rules

1. The application to products lawfully manufactured and marketed in other member states of national legislation prohibiting the marketing of bread with a moisture content exceeding 34 percent or an ash content lower than 1.4 percent or containing bran content constitutes a measure having an effect equivalent to a quantitative restriction within the meaning of article 30 of the EC treaty and is not justified under article 36 of the treaty by the need to protect public health.
2. The national court is under a duty to give full effect to article 30 of the treaty by disapplying on its own initiative provisions of national law conflicting with it.
